headline_o4_int8_verdict.format: O4 contract: signed INT8 [-128,127], no zero point, one BF16 scale per output row applied once after the FP32 K-split sum; embedding and lm_head per vocabulary row; RTN with per-row MSE clip; 8.0033 bits/weight over the matrices (8 + 16/K), 8.0039 embedding
headline_o4_int8_verdict.mode: e_full_w8 (contract arithmetic + FP8 E4M3 KV), tools/qwen3_deployment_quality.py at cf5dbc02 (ran from the byte-identical 25288d25 copy)
headline_o4_int8_verdict.rom: 449.3 mm2 target ROM at 2.001 compute-in-ROM cells/weight: exceeds the 442.6 mm2 ROM + lane-copy pool by 6.7 mm2 before any drafter (64.2 mm2 with an 8-bit drafter)

purpose: Which ROM-shippable Qwen3-8B weight format meets the deployment quality threshold (<= +2% WikiText-2 PPL at 2K and 8K, <= 1.0 pt MMLU drop vs vendor BF16), and what it costs in ROM. Follows results/quality/qwen3_8b_deployment_arithmetic.json, where the 3.5-bit INT3/INT6 stand-in failed.
tool: tools/qwen3_weight_format_search.py (formats, quantisers, capacity) on the harness tools/qwen3_deployment_quality.py (same WikiText-2 windows, same 1,000-question MMLU subset, same threshold); the O4 w8 verdict is tools/qwen3_deployment_quality.py --mode e_full_w8 at cf5dbc02 (byte-identical to 25288d25, the copy that ran)
user_decision: Qwen3-8B uses 8-bit weights (2026-09-28): sub-8-bit formats are rejected on accuracy. The sub-8-bit search below is kept as the record of why; it was stopped when the decision was made (runs in flight were killed, so some screens lack 8K/contract legs).

protocol.reference: a_bf16: vendor BF16 GPU arithmetic, BF16 weights and KV (re-run here: WikiText-2 2K PPL 9.726, 8K 8.549, MMLU 74.7%; identical to the earlier study)
protocol.deployment_verdict_mode: contract arithmetic (golden 45762e32 emulated exactly, reciprocal saturation) + per-element FP8 E4M3 KV; WikiText-2 2K on all 146 windows, 8K on 16 of 36 windows (as the earlier study's contract runs), MMLU 1,000-question subset. Verdict 'acceptable'/'not acceptable' only for this mode with all three measured.
protocol.screen_mode: GPU BF16 arithmetic, BF16 KV, WikiText-2 2K (146 windows) + MMLU 1,000 (some also 8K, all 36 windows). Labelled 'screen' in verdict; the contract + FP8 KV legs moved results by <= ~0.1 pt PPL where both exist (f1 vs s18m/s18).
protocol.cis: paired bootstrap over windows (PPL) and questions (MMLU), 2,000 resamples, 95%
protocol.calibration: GPTQ/Fisher: C4 en shard 00000, 128 x 2,048 tokens (seed 0); Fisher pass 32 x 1,024 (seed 1). RTN formats are data-free.

methods_tried_sub_8_bit.gptq: static groups (scales fixed before the sweep, contiguous groups in ROM), act-order sweep, 1% damp, sequential through already-quantised layers
methods_tried_sub_8_bit.mixed_precision: true sensitivity allocation: group benefit = F_out[n] * sum_k E[x_k^2] (e_lo^2 - e_hi^2), empirical output Fisher x input second moment from one backward pass, ranked globally or per matrix. It put ~31-39% of qkv groups, ~9-34% of gate/up, ~4-8% of o/down/lm_head at the high width, peaking in layers 6 and 35.
methods_tried_sub_8_bit.awq: AWQ-style input scaling (alpha grid per matrix): worse than plain GPTQ at INT4 g128 (+3.87% vs +3.66%).
methods_tried_sub_8_bit.rotation: randomised Hadamard folded into ROM (residual stream + per-head V/O: zero datapath cost given the contract's norm fold; costs +0.20% PPL alone from BF16 re-rounding of rotated weights) and an online FWHT of the down-projection input (blocks of 4,096; a new datapath unit).
methods_tried_sub_8_bit.codebook: fixed global Lloyd-Max Gaussian codebook (lm3/lm4/lm5, levels on the INT8 grid) with a BF16 scale per group: a 2^b-entry LUT per weight ahead of the multiplier. Best 4-bit element type.
methods_tried_sub_8_bit.vector_quantisers: AQLM/QuIP#-style vector codebooks were not implemented (need codebook training/fine-tuning); not run.
findings: 3.5 bits: best is Fisher-global INT3/INT6 + rotation: +6.8% PPL, -4.6 pt MMLU (was +13.8% / -6.2 pt GPTQ); Lloyd-Max 3/6: +5.1% / -5.2 pt. Not close.
~4.1 bits: lm4 g128 + rotation (res+vo+down) +1.95% 2K GPU; in the deployment mode +1.55% 2K but +2.26% 8K and -1.3 pt MMLU: fails.
4.5 bits: lm4 + 10% INT8 groups (Fisher) +1.2..1.5% PPL but MMLU -1.2 to -1.5 pt: fails on MMLU.

5.1 bits: lm5 g128 + rotation +0.63% / -0.5 pt (screen): passes; but a 5-bit element takes two <=4-bit compute-in-ROM cells, so it costs as much ROM as 8 bits. lm4 + 25% INT8 (5.13 bits, 288 mm2) +0.7..1.4% PPL but -1.5..-2.6 pt MMLU: fails.

6.1 bits: lm4 + 50% INT8 (Fisher global): +0.63% / +0.74% PPL, -0.6 pt MMLU (GPU arithmetic, all windows): passes the screen at 344 mm2 target ROM, fits the reticle with no lane copies (m = 1); not run in the deployment mode.
MMLU is the binding criterion from 4 to 5 bits: formats that pass PPL still lose 1.2-2.9 pt.

eight_bit_candidates.rtn_only: All 8-bit candidates are RTN (per-row/per-group MSE-optimal clip, data-free); GPTQ was not needed because RTN passes.
eight_bit_candidates.o4_int8_contract: e_full_w8_o4_contract_25288d25 = THE contract Codex's RTL implements (docs/ARCH_QWEN3_O4_RTL_SPEC.md 3.1): signed INT8 [-128,127], no zero point, one BF16 scale per output row (and per vocabulary row for embedding and lm_head), norm folded into q/k/v and gate/up, FP32 sum in the golden K-split order then one RNE multiply by the row scale, result FP32.
eight_bit_candidates.own_emulation_of_it: e8_int8sym_perchannel_postscale_rtn_contract_fp8: the same arithmetic from this tool, codes restricted to [-127,127]; agrees with the O4 run to within the bootstrap CIs.
eight_bit_candidates.others: e8_int8_g128 (INT8, BF16 scale per 128 along K, applied per element), e8_fp8e4m3_perchannel (E4M3 elements = golden to_fp8, BF16 scale per row, per element).
eight_bit_candidates.note_on_the_int8_per_channel_gain: Per-row INT8 LOWERS perplexity by ~1.5% (2K) / ~1.0% (8K), CI excluding 0, with 95.5% top-1 agreement (INT8 g128: -0.3%, 96.2%; BF16 contract: -0.14%, 98.3%). The weights moved measurably (per-row MSE clipping cuts outlier weights); it is not noise-level identity. It passes the threshold, whose PPL criterion is one-sided; MMLU is -0.3 pt.

rom_capacity.model: compute-in-ROM cell rule of src/opentallas/roofline.py (CimCellAccounting, rom.cim_bits_per_cell = 4, N6 36.48 M cells/mm2, scales at full cell width), 8,190,735,360 ROM-resident parameters incl. embedding; pool for target ROM + drafter ROM + lane copies = 442.6 mm2 on the 815 mm2 reticle (tools/arch_budget_qwen3.py area_ledger with the 261.98 mm2 target ROM of the 3.5-bit design point).
rom_capacity.eight_bit: An 8-bit element takes 2 select cells: INT8 per-row 2.001 cells/weight -> 449.3 mm2 target ROM (+187.3 mm2 over the 3.5-bit design's 261.98); INT8 g128 456.1 mm2. The target ROM alone exceeds the 442.6 mm2 pool by 6.7 mm2 (per-row) / 13.5 mm2 (g128); with the DFlash drafter also 8-bit (57.5 mm2) the deficit is 64.2 / 71.9 mm2 and no lane copies remain (m 3 -> 0). 8-bit weights do NOT fit the single-reticle budget as modelled: something must give (drafter off-die or at fewer bits, the 60 mm2 of HBM PHYs, the compute/overhead shares, or a denser ROM cell).
rom_capacity.weight_sweep: The sweep is one weight per MAC lane per cycle (57,740 cycles/token, 19,027 tok/s ceiling), independent of bits; the ROM read width grows 57,344 -> 131,072 B/cycle, and read + delivery energy 1.03 -> 2.35 mJ/token (+0.29 mJ per bit), small against ~88 mJ/token dominated by KV. KV (the 604 MB/token FP8 stream at 8K) stays the binding resource; 8,910 tok/s at batch 1 is unchanged IF the ROM fits.
rom_capacity.sub_8_bit_reference: 4.125-bit lm4 g128: 231.6 mm2 (fits, m = 3); 6.13-bit lm4+50% INT8: 344.3 mm2 (fits, m = 1); 5.125-bit anything: 456.1 mm2 (does not fit: a 5-bit element costs 2 cells).

datapath.int8_per_row_o4: Cheapest: the lane multiplies INT8 code x BF16 activation (8 x 8 significant bits, exact in FP32) instead of BF16 x BF16, accumulates in FP32 as today, and ONE FP32 multiply per output row applies the scale after the K-split sum (the tree/drain, not the lane). No per-element scale multiply, no decode logic. Compute-in-ROM: an 8-bit weight spans two 4-bit select cells (two partial-product lines, a shift-add of the two nibble products per lane).
datapath.int8_g128: Scale changes every 128 K: either a per-element scale multiply (the lane sees code x scale x activation, 23 significant bits, still exact in FP32) or partial sums per group scaled and added (breaks the golden's single chunk order unless chunks align to 128). More datapath than per-row; no quality reason to prefer it here.
datapath.fp8_e4m3_per_row: Reuses the FP8 E4M3 decode that the KV path already has (E4M3 x BF16 products exact in FP32), scale after the sum as for INT8; slightly worse PPL (+0.5/+0.7%) than INT8 per-row. An FP8 x BF16 lane multiplier is wider in exponent handling than INT8 x BF16.
datapath.sub_8_bit_cost_if_revisited: codebook formats: a 16-entry LUT per lane (tiny); online down-projection Hadamard: an FWHT unit (12,288 x 12 add/sub per token per layer, ~0.3% of the layer's MACs but a new block); residual/VO rotations: free (folded into ROM and the embedding).

not_run: Sub-8-bit contract + FP8 KV legs except lm4 g128 (the search was stopped by the 8-bit decision).
